messages.subject: Unnesting hierarchical data
parts:
I'm stuck, and Google hasn't helped me yet.

I have data in this format:

testdata <- data.frame(
    a = c(' ', '1', '2', '3', ' ', '14', '15'),
    b = c(' ', 'a', '', '', '',  'b', ''),
    c = c(' ', 'A', 'B', 'C', ' ', 'N', 'O'),
    d = c(' ', 'X', 'Y', 'Z', ' ', 'y', 'z'),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


I'd like to get it into this format:

desired <- data.frame(
    P1 = c('1', '1', '14'),
    P2 = c('a', 'a', 'b'),
    P3 = c('A', 'A', 'N'),
    P4 = c('X', 'X', 'y'),
    C1 = c('2', '3', '15'),
    C2 = c('B', 'C', 'O'),
    C3 = c('Y', 'Z', 'z'),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


As is probably obvious, an entry in column b of testdata signifies a parent record, which is always preceded by a blank line.  I want to associate the parent information with each of the children and drop the parent lines.  My test data set has about 60K lines and about 20 columns (parents and children have slightly different numbers of columns).  I'm told a full data set may have a million rows.  Each parent may have a different number of children.

How to flatten hierarchise with awk seems to come close to what I want, but that's awk, and I can't see a way to do something similar in R. 

Any suggestions?

Thanks,

Bill

messages.subject: Re: Unnesting hierarchical data
parts:
fill works on cells with NA, not blank cells (d'uh). 

From http://stackoverflow.com/questions/24172111/change-the-blank-cells-to-na:

empty_as_na <- function(x){
    if("factor" %in% class(x)) x <- as.character(x) ## since ifelse wont work with factors
    ifelse(as.character(x)!="", x, NA)
}
result <- testdata %>%
    mutate(rn = row_number()) %>%
    mutate_each(funs(empty_as_na)) %>% fill(b)

Since there are no unique fields in the parent records, I can't group_by, though.

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Unnesting hierarchical data
parts:
This is how I would do it:

parents = apply(testdata, 1, function(x) all(!grepl('\\w|\\d', x)))
testdata$parent = cumsum(parents)
parentdata = testdata[which(parents) + 1, ]
childdata = testdata[-c(which(parents), which(parents) + 1), ]
merge(parentdata, childdata, by = 'parent')

I'll leave it to you to find a fancy dplyr/tidyr way to do it. The key to this approach is constructing a parent id in the original data so you can match parents and children again after splitting them up.

Best,
Ista

for (i in 1:nrows) {

    ## Write recordcount into recordnum field.

}

parents <- testdata %>%
    group_by(recordnum) %>%
    slice(1)
colnames(parents) <- c(c('a','b','c','d'),'recordnum')
parents <- parents

children <- testdata %>%
    group_by(recordnum) %>%
    ## Delete parent row and blank separator row.

children <- children %>%
    dplyr::select(-starts_with('X'))

results <- parents %>%

That's not quite right; my real versionhas a row of parent headers and then a row of child headers, and I carried those along and put them in the right places.  This code also has a small defect I don't have time to find right now; it seems to miss the second record, and the numbers are incremented by 1, neither of which happen in my production code.

Thanks for your contribution.
